text:
- chief complaint: right groin and hip pain.
- history of present illness: right hip pain since february 2020, first triggered by stepping back while walking, now with any movement. Pivoting causes catching, sometimes with falls. Pain ranges 2 to 7 out of 10 and improves with rest. Imaging showed high-grade chondromalacia of the right acetabulum.
- physical examination: blood pressure 115/75, pulse 67. Gait and toe and heel walking intact. Neck and low back are painless with full range of motion. Right hip range of motion is decreased, with groin pain on rotation and resisted flexion. Trochanter non-tender. Motor normal, reflexes 1+, no focal deficits.
- symptoms experienced by the patient: right groin pain, catching, falls, pain with pivoting. No fever, chills, numbness, tingling, or bowel or bladder changes.
- new medications prescribed or changed, including dosages: NSAIDs as needed (dosage N/A). Cortisone injection into the right hip joint given today (dosage N/A).
- follow-up instructions: low-impact exercise handout, cane use to offload the right side, return in three months for a repeat injection if needed.
